repl.description: Start an interactive NestJS REPL for Meanderaw services

start.description: Run the Meanderaw application. With no arguments it sweeps every meander into output/meanders.sqlite — the whole lattice's unit space, enumerated and classified, then the historical corpus's hardcoded Codes beyond that budget; with --args="--rows <n> --columns <n> --code <code>" it writes that one row; with --args="--check" it regenerates that same sweep into a throwaway database and fails if it disagrees with the committed one, which `sweep-check` runs (no longer wired into `lint-codebase`, so it must be run directly). `build` compiles this project rather than drawing anything, so populating the database is this target's job.

sweep-check.description: Regenerate the whole sweep — the generalized enumeration and the historical corpus's hardcoded ingestion, exactly what a real sweep runs — into a throwaway in-memory database, and diff it against the committed output/meanders.sqlite, failing on any new, missing, or changed row. This is what catches drift in the generic renderer, the enumerator, or a Characteristic's own logic before it reaches the committed corpus, the same CI role `address-table` once played for the retired per-family procedural pipeline. Deliberately uncached, for the same reason that target was: it reads the committed database rather than any declared build output, so caching it buys nothing while a stale hit could hide real drift — and the sweep itself costs under a minute, not the hours a cache exists to save. `--check` is a boolean flag rather than a `check`/`write` configuration pair, unlike `address-table`: nothing here can "fix" drift by rewriting the committed database from a branch, since that database is populated by a real `start` run a person chooses to make, not by an aggregator's own `--configuration=write`.
